text:
Incident Bot: 🚨 RESOLVED: elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate (region: us-west-2). Mitigation applied at 2026-06-15T14:12:10Z. Full timeline and auto page: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-3425

Alex Torres: I'm the on-call. Quick summary: around 14:02 UTC we saw a spike in 502/504s after a bad rollout of a routing change. We rolled traffic back to the previous routing policy at 14:10 and error rate dropped to baseline by 14:12.

Jamie Li: Adding initial timeline here so we have it in-thread:
- 13:56 UTC: deploy of routing tweak (traffic split rules)
- 14:01 UTC: first pager, 30% 5xx on /v1/generate
- 14:06 UTC: traffic steering attempt -> increased errors
- 14:10 UTC: rollback to previous routing config
- 14:12 UTC: errors back to normal

Maya R.: Customer impact: two enterprise customers on dedicated pools reported increased error rates; most hosted traffic saw elevated latency but not complete failures. I flagged CS leads and asked EM to prepare a bridge offer if customers request.

Emily Chan: Confirmed — I've opened a support case for acct 4521 and scheduled a follow-up ping for 16:00 PDT today. We should prepare an RCA summary and a customer-facing timeline.

Alex Torres: Ops notes: the rollback was manual (kubectl apply on routing-config), see command I ran: 
```
kubectl apply -f routing-configs/routing-2026-06-15-previous.yaml 
# apply returned: configmap "routing-config" configured
```
Logs near failure: 
```
2026-06-15T14:01:23Z ERROR inference-proxy: upstream 10.2.4.8: read: connection reset by peer status=502 request_id=abc123
2026-06-15T14:03:19Z ERROR inference-proxy: kv-cache miss storm, latencies spiked to 1.5s
```

Nora Patel: I reproduced locally with the routing change. The reproducer is: toggle split to route 20% to new path and run long sequence load -> cache priming fails and proxies drop connections. I put notes in the repro doc: https://confluence.redwood.example/repro/INC-3425.

Jamie Li: Root cause hypothesis (tentative): routing change exposed a path with a cache hot-spot and slightly different keepalive settings on that backend. Under load the backend started resetting connections; the proxy treated resets as 502 and retried in a way that amplified load. We'll validate with kernel tcp settings, keepalive, and proxy retry behavior.

Ops Bot: runbook invoked: routing-rollback (version v2). Runbook steps executed: notify, rollback, verify. Duration: 00:10:12.

Sam O'Neill: Can we schedule a post-incident review? I think a 60-minute postmortem to finalize RCA and action items. My availability tomorrow 09:00-11:00 UTC or 15:00-17:00 UTC.

Jamie Li: I'm good for tomorrow 15:00 UTC. Alex can lead the mitigation portion, Nora to cover repro, and I will draft the technical RCA.

Alex Torres: Prefer 15:00 UTC as well. Suggest we invite SRE, runtime eng, product, and CS (Emily + Maya).

Maya R.: I'll prepare a short customer-facing timeline draft. Proposal for customer comms (to be reviewed):
> Hi — we identified a routing configuration change that caused elevated errors for some requests to /v1/generate between 14:01–14:12 UTC. We rolled back the change which restored normal service. We are performing a full RCA and will share a timeline and remediation plan by EOD tomorrow. If you'd like a private bridge, we'll schedule one.

Emily Chan: That draft looks good. Please add an explicit apology and note any short-term mitigations we're offering (credits or SLA exceptions) depending on impact.

Jamie Li: Action items (proposed):
- ACTION-3425-1: Finalize RCA document (owner: Jamie Li) — due: 2026-06-16T18:00:00Z
- ACTION-3425-2: Postmortem meeting (owner: Sam O'Neill to schedule) — proposed: 2026-06-16T15:00 UTC
- ACTION-3425-3: Update routing runbook to include the cache-priming checklist (owner: Nora Patel) — due: 2026-06-23
- ACTION-3425-4: Customer comms & status page update (owner: Emily Chan) — draft by 2026-06-15T23:00 PDT
- ACTION-3425-5: Add automated canary checks for keepalive/regression (owner: Jamie Li + Eng Runtime) — due: 2026-07-01

Alex Torres: I'll add a short note to the incident page with exact rollback commands and verification steps.

Nora Patel: For the runbook update, I'll include the reproducer snippet and a recommended traffic-steering ramp pattern (5% -> 10% -> 25% with checks).

Maya R.: For customer-facing RCA, can we include a short "what we're doing to prevent this" list: 1) stricter routing rollout ramp, 2) keepalive/retry tuning, 3) automated canaries for KV cache priming. Emily, I'll attach the draft to the support case.

Emily Chan: On status page: I have a draft that summarizes incident and resolution. Status Page link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/INC-3425-digest — I'll post once Jamie drops the RCA summary.

Jamie Li: I'll aim to post an internal technical RCA by 18:00 UTC and a customer-facing summary by 23:00 local (PDT).

Sam O'Neill: I'll create the calendar invite for 2026-06-16T15:00 UTC and add the agenda: timeline, root cause, action items, owner signoff.

Alex Torres: Quick checklist before we close thread: confirm customer comm draft, confirm postmortem invite, set owners in tracking board. Once those are done, I'll close the incident page. :white_check_mark:

Maya R.: Confirmed — I'll update the support case and ping customers after the RCA is ready.

Incident Bot: Reminder set: postmortem invite scheduled by Sam O'Neill. Next automated check-in in 24h.

Emily Chan: :thumbsup: thanks everyone — will coordinate the customer follow-ups.
